description: Output quality eval: verify ue-pre-commit produces staged-change analysis with BP impact assessment and risk level verdict

assertions.description: Should reference staged/changed files when present, OR correctly report no staged C++ changes on a clean tree (Issue #16685: clean-tree robust — clean-tree phrasing varies run-to-run, so accept both vocab sets; an off-topic answer still matches none)

Should detect staged changes via git, and/or analyze them via ue_analyze_symbols. On a clean tree the skill short-circuits at git change-detection and never reaches the impact phase (Issue #16493: clean-tree robust; ue_analyze_symbols requires a real tool call — git may also be credited from the report text, so on-topic signal is enforced by the sibling content_contains_any/llm_judge assertions and the harness MCP-reachability gate)

assertions.criteria: Does the response analyze the staged changes and assess commit safety — identifying what was changed and whether it is safe to commit — OR, when no C++ files are staged, correctly report that there is nothing to commit / safe to commit? Either a concrete staged-change safety assessment OR an explicit 'nothing staged / safe to commit' verdict passes. A vague, off-topic, or non-commit-safety answer fails.
assertions.description: Should provide commit safety assessment OR correctly report no staged changes (LLM judge; clean-tree robust, Issue #16493)
Should address commit safety — risk/safety vocab when changes are staged, OR clean-tree 'nothing to commit' phrasing (Issue #16685: clean-tree robust)

assertions.criteria: Does the response provide a clear yes/no verdict on commit safety with supporting evidence from code analysis — OR, when no C++ files are staged, correctly state there is nothing to commit and that it is safe to commit? Either a verdict backed by change analysis OR an explicit clean-tree 'nothing staged / safe' verdict passes. A vague or off-topic answer fails.
assertions.description: Should provide clear safety verdict OR correctly report no staged changes (LLM judge; clean-tree robust, Issue #16493)

assertions.criteria: Does the response either (a) identify which Blueprints/assets are affected by the staged C++ changes — naming BPs, cross-references, or C++→BP dependencies — OR (b), when no C++ files are staged, correctly report that there is nothing to analyze / no affected Blueprints? Either a concrete affected-BP impact analysis OR an explicit 'no staged changes / no impact' verdict passes. A vague, off-topic, or non-impact answer fails.
